candidate_properties.title: In-place coefficient-wise addition preserves exact old-state/new-state relation under overflow-free assumptions
candidate_properties.candidate_statement: For mlk_poly_add(mlk_poly *r, const mlk_poly *b), under the stated non-aliasing and overflow-preventing preconditions, each coefficient index k in [0, MLKEM_N) satisfies r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k] after the call, and only r->coeffs is modified.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: /* Add two polynomials in place. ... The coefficients of @p r and @p b must be such that the addition does not overflow. Otherwise, the behaviour of this function is undefined. ... @param[in,out] r Input-output polynomial to be added to. @param[in]     b Input polynomial that should be added to @p r. Must be disjoint from @p r. */ ... requires(memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(forall(k0, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] + b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX)) requires(forall(k1, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN)) ensures(forall(k, 0, MLKEM_N, r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k])) assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly)))
